claims.text: The proposed learning algorithm achieves group fairness by ensuring the proportion of protected group members receiving positive classification equals that of the overall population.
The proposed learning algorithm achieves individual fairness by treating similar individuals similarly.
Fairness can be formulated as an optimization problem of finding a data representation that balances data encoding quality with protected group membership obfuscation.
Intermediate representations learned for fair classification can be transferred to other classification tasks.
The fair representation formulation enables learning a distance metric to identify important data dimensions for classification.

evidence.description: We propose a learning algorithm for fair classification that achieves both group fairness (the proportion of members in a protected group receiving positive classification is identical to the proportion in the population as a whole)
achieves... individual fairness (similar individuals should be treated similarly)

We formulate fairness as an optimization problem of finding a good representation of the data with two competing goals: to encode the data as well as possible, while simultaneously obfuscating any information about membership in the protected group.
our intermediate representation can be used for other classification tasks (i.e., transfer learning is possible)
we take a step toward learning a distance metric which can find important dimensions of the data for classification

methodologies.name: Learning Fair Representations
methodologies.description: An optimization-based learning algorithm that constructs data representations to maximize reconstruction quality while obfuscating protected group membership.
